declarations.docstring: The auxiliary invariant of a multivariate polynomial ring over a field equals the number of variables.
Transfers the auxiliary degree-indexed property across a ring equivalence.
The auxiliary property in degree d for a commutative ring implies it in degree d + 1 for its polynomial ring.
A small semisimple ring satisfies the auxiliary property in degree zero.
An equivalence of abelian categories preserves the bound on projective dimension.
A multivariate polynomial ring in n variables over a field satisfies the auxiliary property in degree n.
If a multivariate polynomial ring over a field has the auxiliary property in degree d, then its number of variables is at most d.
